newsitem.title: USA: HORACE TO TAKE $10MLN RESTRUCTURING CHARGE.
newsitem.headline: HORACE TO TAKE $10MLN RESTRUCTURING CHARGE.

text.p: Horace Small Apparel Plc said Monday it will take charges totaling $8 million to $10 million in the next 12 months to restructure its manufacturing and distribution operations and is considering making shareholders a cash offer of 110 pence ($1.79) a share.

The company said it is in discussions with unnamed parties who "may be interested in making a cash offer to existing shareholders" of 110 pence per share, or $1.79, based on a dollar/sterling exchange rate of US$1.63. It added certain company directors may provide part of the cash offer.
Horace said it is considering cancelling its listing on the London Stock Exchange and seeking a listing on a U.S. market once the restructuring benefits are "reflected in trading performance."

Horace said shareholders need to approve the delisting proposal by ordinary resolution, with directors participating in the cash offer abstaining. The company added it will hire an independent adviser to give a fairness opinion.

The company said the restructuring charges will increase sales and profitability "significantly" over the medium term. It added the charges are in addition to a $2 million charge it earlier announced to close its Guthry operations and start up its Brownsville plant.
The company's stock opened at a 52-week high of 101 pence Monday.
